claim: Google SRE organization caps operational toil at 50% of each SRE's time, with the remaining 50% dedicated to engineering work that reduces future toil or adds service features.
quote: Our SRE organization has an advertised goal of keeping operational work (i.e., toil) below 50% of each SRE's time. At least 50% of each SRE's time should be spent on engineering project work that will either reduce future toil or add service features.

claim: SRE is fundamentally defined as applying software engineering principles to operations — hiring software engineers to run operations and creating systems to accomplish work that would otherwise be manual.
quote: SRE is what happens when you ask a software engineer to design an operations team.

claim: Error budgets resolve the structural conflict between development velocity and system reliability by quantifying acceptable unreliability.
quote: The error budget stems from the observation that 100% is the wrong reliability target for basically everything. In general, for any software service or system, 100% is not the right reliability target because no user can tell the difference between a system being 100% available and 99.999% available.

claim: SLI measures service behavior from the user perspective; SLO attaches SLIs to business value to communicate reliability across the organization.
quote: SLI, or Service Level Indicator, represents a measurement of a service's behavior. A good SLI measures your service from the perspective of your users. SLO, or Service Level Objective, represents the means by which reliability is communicated to an organization/other teams.

claim: Blameless postmortems are essential for incident learning — removing blame gives people confidence to escalate issues without fear, while blame culture drives incidents underground.
quote: Blameless postmortems can be challenging to write, because the postmortem format clearly identifies the actions that led to the incident. Removing blame from a postmortem gives people the confidence to escalate issues without fear. An atmosphere of blame risks creating a culture in which incidents and issues are swept under the rug, leading to greater risk for the organization.

claim: Postmortem triggers should be defined before incidents occur, including user-visible downtime, data loss, on-call intervention, resolution time thresholds, and monitoring failures.
quote: Teams have some internal flexibility, but common postmortem triggers include: User-visible downtime or degradation beyond a certain threshold; Data loss of any kind; On-call engineer intervention; A resolution time above some threshold; A monitoring failure.

claim: Observability is the ability to understand a system's internal state by examining its outputs through three signal types: traces, metrics, and logs.
quote: Observability is the ability to understand the internal state of a system by examining its outputs. In software, this is typically achieved by analyzing telemetry data such as traces, metrics, and logs.

claim: Proper instrumentation means developers don't need to add more instrumentation to troubleshoot issues because all necessary information is already available.
quote: An application is properly instrumented when developers don't need to add more instrumentation to troubleshoot an issue, because they have all of the information they need.

claim: OpenTelemetry provides vendor-neutral instrumentation for traces, metrics, and logs, becoming the de facto standard for observability.
quote: OpenTelemetry is the mechanism by which application code is instrumented to help make a system observable.

claim: An Internal Developer Platform (IDP) is built by platform teams to create golden paths and enable developer self-service, lowering cognitive load without abstracting away context.
quote: An Internal Developer Platform (IDP) is built by a platform team to build golden paths and enable developer self-service. An IDP consists of many different techs and tools, glued together in a way that lowers cognitive load on developers without abstracting away context and underlying technologies.

claim: Platform Orchestrators have become the standard centerpiece of enterprise-grade IDPs, turning disjointed toolchains into cohesive platforms.
quote: Platform Orchestrators are what turn your disjointed toolchain into an enterprise-grade Internal Developer Platform. Platform Orchestrators were mentioned in the last Thoughtworks tech radar, discussed at KubeCon, and are a hot topic amongst leading consultancies.

claim: Successful platform engineering initiatives start small with a Minimum Viable Platform (MVP) approach and iterate quickly to continuously prove value to stakeholders.
quote: Successful platform engineering initiatives start small, following a Minimum Viable Platform (MVP) approach, and iterate quickly to continuously prove value to all key stakeholders.

claim: Platform engineering maturity progresses through levels from initial ad-hoc capabilities to optimizing ecosystems where specialists extend platform capabilities.
quote: Level 4, Optimizing — Enabled ecosystem: It becomes a priority to enable specialists to extend platform capabilities and introduce new ones. The organization can centralize specialists allowing their knowledge and support to be spread through platform capabilities.

claim: Platform adoption typically starts slowly driven by platform builders, then accelerates as users pull adoption once platforms provide enough value.
quote: A common growth pattern for platform adoption showcases the often slow start driven mainly by platform builders. Once platforms provide enough value to users, growth becomes more pulled by the users causing a steeper adoption curve.

claim: Developer portals serve as the interface through which developers discover and access internal developer platform capabilities, but are not the platform itself.
quote: Internal developer portals serve as the interface through which developers can discover and access internal developer platform capabilities. Portals are simply one of the possible interfaces (UI-based specifically) of the underlying platform.

claim: Google's code review process maintains code quality and product quality through systematic examination by someone other than the author.
quote: At Google, we use code review to maintain the quality of our code and products. This documentation is the canonical description of Google's code review processes and policies.

claim: Heavyweight code review processes requiring multiple approvals before merging to trunk create a downward spiral where developers batch changes, making reviews even harder.
quote: Many organizations have a heavyweight code review process that requires multiple approvals before changes can be merged into trunk. When code review is laborious and takes hours or days, developers avoid working in small batches and instead batch up many changes.

claim: Synchronous code reviews (asking someone to review right then) are preferred over asynchronous reviews to minimize merge delays and conflicts.
quote: If further reviews are required, they should be performed synchronously: when the developer is ready to commit the code, they should ask somebody else on the team to review the code right then. They should not ask for asynchronous review.

claim: Agent-generated pull requests require specialized review strategies to catch technical debt, hallucinated APIs, and over-engineered abstractions that AI tends to introduce.
quote: A practical guide to reviewing agent-generated pull requests: what to look for, where issues hide, and how to catch technical debt before it ships.

claim: Continuous Integration requires frequent integration to mainline, not just running CI tools on feature branches — the latter is semantic diffusion that causes confusion.
quote: Because of this Semantic Diffusion, some people started to use the term 'Trunk-Based Development' instead of 'Continuous Integration'. Many organizations that use these tools use them to automatically build feature branches on commit — which, while useful, means they don't actually practice Continuous Integration.

claim: Feature toggles fall into distinct categories (Release, Experiment, Ops, Permission) that should be managed differently even if using the same technical machinery.
quote: There are various categories of Feature Toggles with different characteristics. These differences should be embraced, and different toggles managed in different ways, even if all the various toggles might be controlled using the same technical machinery.

claim: Ops Toggles control operational aspects of system behavior and should be reconfigured extremely quickly to allow operators to react to production issues.
quote: Since the purpose of these flags is to allow operators to quickly react to production issues they need to be re-configured extremely quickly. Many of these flags are only in place for a short while, but a few key controls may be left in place for operators almost indefinitely.

claim: Harness engineering — building specifications, quality checks, and workflow guidance that control AI agents — has emerged as a critical practice for human-AI collaboration in software development.
quote: The collection of specifications, quality checks, and workflow guidance that control different levels of loops inside the how loop is the agent's harness. The emerging practice of building and maintaining these harnesses, Harness Engineering, is how humans work on the loop.

claim: The difference between human-in-the-loop and human-on-the-loop is visible in response to unsatisfactory output: in-the-loop fixes the artifact directly; on-the-loop changes the harness that produces it.
quote: The difference between in the loop and on the loop is most visible in what we do when we're not satisfied with what the agent produces. The 'in the loop' way is to fix the artefact. The 'on the loop' way is to change the harness that produces it.

claim: Canary releases detect problems and regressions by rolling out changes to a subset of users, but should not be conflated with A/B testing which tests hypotheses.
quote: Canary releases can be used as a way to implement A/B testing due to similarities in the technical implementation. However, it is preferable to avoid conflating these two concerns: while canary releases are a good way to detect problems and regressions, A/B testing is a way to test a hypothesis using variant implementations.

claim: The Strangler Fig pattern enables incremental legacy modernization by gradually replacing components while maintaining system operation.
quote: Patterns of Legacy Displacement goes into more detail on using an incremental approach to modernization and is in the process of developing a catalog of patterns to describe useful techniques.

claim: Technical debt should be treated as a first-class backlog citizen with clear acceptance criteria and measurable outcomes such as faster build times or fewer flaky tests.
quote: Treat refactors and technical debt as first-class backlog items. This will provide them with clear acceptance criteria and measurable outcomes, such as faster build times or fewer flaky tests. Set aside time each sprint for maintenance, reliability, and performance work.

claim: Agile teams treat resilience and maintainability as product features, scheduling refactors and practicing blameless incident response to reduce future cycle time.
quote: Agile teams treat resilience and maintainability as product features. Developers schedule refactors, pay down technical debt, and practice blameless incident response. This reduces future cycle time and increases confidence in change.

claim: DORA measures software delivery throughput through change lead time, deployment frequency, and failed deployment recovery time.
quote: DORA uses three factors to measure software delivery throughput: Change lead time (committed to deployed), Deployment frequency (number of deployments over a given period), Failed deployment recovery time (time to recover from a failed deployment).

claim: Version control ensures reproducibility and traceability, serving as a critical safety net as AI accelerates the velocity of change.
quote: Version control ensures reproducibility and traceability, serving as a critical safety net as AI accelerates the velocity of change.

claim: CI/CD pipelines automate the creation, testing, and deployment of applications, reducing errors in the deployment process by catching bugs early.
quote: A CI/CD pipeline is an automated process utilized by software development teams to streamline the creation, testing and deployment of applications. Integrating a CI/CD pipeline into your workflow significantly reduces the risk of errors in the deployment process.

claim: OWASP DevSecOps promotes shift-left security culture by integrating security testing (SAST, SCA, DAST, IaC scanning) early in the development pipeline.
quote: The OWASP DevSecOps Guideline explains how we can implement a secure pipeline and use best practices. The project is trying to help us promote the shift-left security culture in our development process. The ideal goal is 'detect security issues as fast as possible.'

claim: Platform engineering success requires treating the platform as a product with dedicated product management, user research, and iteration based on feedback.
quote: Following best practices, platform teams treat their platform as a product and build it based on user research, maintaining and continuously improving it.

claim: CNCF platform maturity model defines progression from basic capability provisioning to optimizing ecosystems with enabled specialist extensions.
quote: At their most basic, internal platforms provide consistent experiences for acquiring and using individual services. As they mature, internal platforms also offer compositions of such services as self-serviceable templates for key scenarios.

claim: Platform success metrics include user satisfaction (NPS), active users and retention, and developer productivity metrics from the SPACE framework.
quote: Metrics that reflect user satisfaction and productivity include: Active users and retention, Net Promoter Score (NPS), Metrics for developer productivity such as those discussed in the SPACE framework.

claim: Evolutionary architectures support modularity and well-defined boundaries that enable non-breaking changes, while inappropriate coupling inhibits evolution by propagating changes unpredictably.
quote: The ability to separate components along well defined boundaries has obvious benefit if a developer wants to make a non-breaking change. Inappropriate coupling inhibits evolution by propagating changes in difficult to predict ways.

claim: Microservice teams favor open standards developed through live implementations over rigid corporate standards that lack recent programming experience.
quote: The key difference is how the standards are developed and how they are enforced. Standards managed by groups such as the IETF only become standards when there are several live implementations of them in the wider world.

claim: Closing the data feedback loop from production enables continuous improvement by adapting models based on learnings from real production data.
quote: By capturing this data, you can close the data feedback loop. Closing this feedback loop is one of the main advantages of CD4ML, as it allows us to adapt our models based on learnings taken from real production data, creating a process of continuous improvement.

claim: Manual verification provides higher confidence that features behave as intended, complementing automated test coverage.
quote: We manually verify that our code works as expected. Automated test coverage is essential, but manual verification provides a higher level of confidence that features behave as intended and bugs are fixed.

claim: Pull requests add process to mainline pushes but can create significant friction for continuous integration when reviews take hours or days.
quote: The pre-integration code review can be problematic for Continuous Integration because it usually adds significant friction to the integration process. Instead of an automated process that can be done within minutes, we have to find someone to do the code review, schedule their time, and wait for feedback.

claim: Pair programming creates continuous real-time code review as code is being written, producing a much faster feedback loop than asynchronous PR reviews.
quote: Pair Programming is popular because it creates a continuous real-time code review as the code is being written, producing a much faster feedback loop for the review.

claim: Engineering work in SRE is novel, requires human judgment, produces permanent improvements, and enables the team to handle larger services with the same staffing.
quote: Engineering work is novel and intrinsically requires human judgment. It produces a permanent improvement in your service, and is guided by a strategy. Engineering work helps your team or the SRE organization handle a larger service, or more services, with the same level of staffing.
